I would like to PR a proof of SL n R = E n R for R a local ring, euclidean domain, ring of integers of number fields, ecc.. , in order to refactor the existing proof of SL 2 ℤ being f.g. and prove it for general n. My approach is to follow : H. Bass, "K-theory and stable algebra" for the proof.
Is someone already working on that?
I am doing that as it seems to me the best route to have that the map SL 2 ℤ → SL ZMod N is surjective as I do not find very beautiful the ad hoc argument building the precise lift.
So far I have refactored the pivot reducing argument in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Transvection to work with a commutative ring. If you think this is an interesting I will open the refactor PR and continue to work on the proof of SL n R = E n R.

I think a good option would be to refactor Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/SpecialLinearGroup by deleting the sections on trnsvection and move them in a new file introducing also the definition of the elementary subgroup as a subgroup of SL and then refactor the proofs using commutative rings instead of fields and proving the analog of exists_list_transvec_mul_diagonal_mul_list_transvec for rings satisfying the stable range condition with n = 1 (so without the need of also define the notion of stable range as it would work only with unimodularity). This already would cover local rings and euclidean domain for all n.
Do you think this could be a good approach?
This PR #44314 proposes a version of the elementary subgroup and a proves E(n,R) = SL(n, R) for local rings.

Looked into the repos following the announcement #Autoformalization > Formal Frontier Libraries @ 💬 citing Weibel's K-book as a source; the developments seem to be happening in https://github.com/FormalFrontier/general-linear-groups

Looking at the readme there's no definition of higher K-groups; I wrote up a definition using Quillen's Q-construction with sorries which Aristotle was able to fill:
KGroup.lean (with sorries)
https://aristotle.harmonic.fun/projects/a37f97cb-5f27-4d54-86b5-7b6e746ba55c (sorry free)
I plan to use it to state some challenge(s) in LeanEval.
(Edit: oh, I forgot it has been done at #general > O(1000) definitions for Annals @ 💬 )
Do you know whether they plan to PR some of their results?
The Formal Frontier Libraries repos? No such plan as far as I'm aware.
